prior_diagnostic_no_go.finding: Both guarded arms were technically complete, but the only two depot spare demands were both TEACH-LRU-01. MINBS2 batched same-IID items; mixed-IID acceptance failed. Raw runs retained as diagnostics and not published.

second_diagnostic_no_go.finding: Two mixed-IID demand pairs produced four total depot demands, exceeding the prior exactly-two-demand gate. Native raw retained; this finding motivated a separate four-demand contract with fresh guarded runs.

third_diagnostic_no_go.finding: One scheduled mission produced only one depot demand, so it could not test a two-piece threshold. Native raw retained and not published.

source.interpretation: Manual p255 requires the sum of sub-item failure rates not to exceed the mother System failure rate; two 3,000,000-hour LRU rates therefore require System.FRT 6,000,000 in both arms. Manual p336 permits different items in a batch when their transport data match between the same stations. Two independently traceable demand pairs, each containing both IID values, and two physical two-item tasks must appear in the native ledger before claiming mixed batching. The seed-2 two-mission topology is known from the rejected v1.0.1 diagnostic; this v1.0.3 contract is explicit about that provenance and requires fresh guarded replay.

predeclared_native_acceptance: Derive both arms only from their accepted E10.var06 same-item MINBS counterparts. Clone TEACH-LRU-01 as TEACH-LRU-02 in Item, ItemStructure, ItemRepair and the two StockAllocation rows; preserve their quantities, location, failure/repair parameters and the same general StationStructure link. Set System.FRT to 6,000,000 in both arms to satisfy manual p255. Change Control.RSEED from 1 to 2 and ProblemDescription. No other tables, mission, policy or time changes are allowed.

Under frozen seed 2 and two scheduled missions, native events must show exactly four depot spare demands at exactly two distinct event times, each time with one TEACH-LRU-01 and one TEACH-LRU-02 on the same depot-to-base transport link. Each demand must map to one physical depot spare. Any other count, item mix or link is NO-GO for v1.0.3.

With MINBS1, the four demands must make four separate one-item downward tasks, with no mixed two-item task. With MINBS2, each same-time mixed-IID pair must make one physical two-item downward task; the first provisional one-item task is cancelled or held before departure, and both item IDs start and arrive together after two hours. This is a structural batch comparison at simultaneous demand times; no waiting-time improvement is claimed. An early one-item MINBS2 departure, missing item, extra downward task or different transport data is NO-GO.

Reconcile individual failures, item identities and depot/base inventory, all transport tasks including upward failed-item returns, repair/restock, backorders and waits, mission outcomes, 72 half-hour system/stock report bins and terminal readiness/backorder/in-transit state for both arms. Report aggregate equality or differences precisely; do not infer mixed batching from totals alone.

Use guarded session-0 SSH under Global\SimloxIssue18NativeQueue with fresh unique run IDs. Preserve GUI PID13340, roundtrip every authored populated table, require zero conversion errors and nonempty SXO/log/report, seal source and raw SHA-256 and obtain independent read-only replay without importing the author's checker.
limits: One fixed seed, two aircraft, two item types, one general depot-to-base transport link and MINBS threshold two. No separate ItemStationStructure transport data, system transport, cross-link pooling, larger thresholds, partial horizon batch, GUI visuals or cross-engine parity.

Prior v1.0.0, v1.0.1 and v1.0.2 diagnostics all failed their own immutable contracts and remain unpublished. v1.0.3 repeats the v1.0.1 model under a separately frozen four-demand contract and new run IDs; full E10, E11 and Issue #18 remain open.
